description: STAGE-CONSISTENCY BASELINE for saga #811 (issue #816 item 5): the `check()` half of a pair whose `-execute` sibling WAS a characterization fixture and is now a `REGRESSION WALL` — issue #815 flipped it, and no characterization fixture remains in the corpus. This half is ALREADY CORRECT today and is expected to survive the fix UNCHANGED — it was precisely the answer the run path never consulted, which was the whole of saga #811's shape-A mechanism. Issue #815 made the run consult it, so the sibling changed and this half did not — which is what the pair was built to demonstrate. Fault shape A — an UNRESOLVABLE NAME in argument position. `check()` computes the right answer (`ol-unknown-command`, whose usual stage is `semantic` per spec/error-model.md:97). At the time this fixture was written `execute()` never consulted it, so the statement was discarded whole with no diagnostic and no effect; measured after issue #815, the same program reports that `ol-unknown-command` and emits zero events. This half is unchanged either way, which is the point of a stage-consistency baseline. One diagnostic, on the recursive call's argument. NOTE on provenance: this is NOT the maintainer's `PLANT` fractal that issue #816 item 3 names — that source is not in this repository, so its inherited 5-vs-6,253 draw-segment numbers are asserted nowhere in this slice. This is a minimal recursive tree written for this fixture, and every number its `-execute` sibling asserts was measured from it.
